div.head: III Atr 3.2
div.ab: Et capiantur accusati, qui cum preposito causam habent, et omnis eorum det VI dimidias marcas uadii, dimidium domino ipsius terre, dimidium wapentako.
⁊ niman þonne þa tihtbysian men, þe mid þam gerefan habbað, ⁊ heora ælc sylle VI healfmarc wedd, healf landrícan ⁊ healf wǽpentake.
⁊ niman þonne þa tihtbysian men þe mid þam gerefan [sace] habbað, ⁊ heora ælc sylle VI healfmarc wedd, healf landrícan ⁊ healf wǽpentake.

And then they shall arrest those men of bad repute against whom the reeve is taking proceedings, and each of them shall pay six half marks as security, half to the lord of the manor, and half to the wapentake.

And they are then to seize the men who have frequently been accused, against whom the reeve is taking proceedings, and each of them is to pay six half marks as pledge, half to the lord of the estate and half to the wapentake.

und sie sollen ferner die bescholtenen Leute, die bei dem [gerichtsherrlichen] Vogte [eine Strafsache hängen] haben, greifen, und deren jeder zahle 6 Halbmark Pfand, halb dem Immunitätsherrn und halb dem Wapentake.

and they are further to seize the men of bad repute who have [a case pending] with the [lord's] reeve, and let each of them give 6 half-marks as pledge, half to the lord of the immunity and half to the wapentake.
div.note: Editors supply ‘sace’ after ‘gerefan’ in H from Quadr.'s ‘causam’.
The Old English text is corrupt here; this rendering (which is Miss Robert son’s) is based on Quadripartitus.
